title: the WSG grappling hooks
audit_label: R444 WSG grappling hooks pin audit
audit_comment: The grappling-hooks slice pins the 1/3-of-strength rounded-up times-10-feet throw (Str 8 = 30 feet), the horizontal throw (same as vertical on a 30-degree-or-less incline, doubled from a secure position with a 10-foot whirling radius), the one-round throw with the 1d4-round re-coil on a miss, the 01-05 self-hit for 1d6 damage on a missed throw directly above, the 3-foot climb bonus for the unencumbered, Table 20 GRAPPLING SUCCESS (10 terrain rows x the protrusion pair and the non-slippery/slightly slippery/slippery catch chances), the solid vs not-solid protrusion procedure (solid holds indefinitely, not-solid gives way after 1d6 rounds of climbing) and the recheck-after-10-feet rule (rules/wsggrap.h, prefix wgh); census 368 -> 369.

banner.title: The WSG USE OF GRAPPLING HOOKS, R444: the hook prose and Table 20 - the other piece of equipment any climber can use (thief or non-thief, mountaineer or not) is a grappling hook, a three- or four-pronged metal hook attached to the end of a rope and thrown toward a protrusion in hopes it catches and holds. Hooks are normally needed only for severe slopes and cliff faces but expedite a moderate slope, especially a slippery one. A character throws a hook upward a maximum of 1/3 of his strength score (rounded up) times 10 feet - strength 8 reaches 30 feet above the head. A horizontal throw (a 30-degree-or-less incline) matches the vertical distance unless the thrower is in a secure position with a 10-foot whirling radius, in which case he throws twice as far. A throw takes one round; a miss costs the next 1d4 rounds coiling the rope. A missed throw at a target directly above with a roll of 01-05 hits the thrower for 1d6 damage. Climbing an anchored rope gives a 3-foot bonus to the climbing movement rate if lightly or not encumbered, otherwise no movement benefit. Table 20 pairs the Chance of Protrusion (a percentile roll at or above the first number means a protrusion exists; at or above the second it is solid and holds indefinitely; between the two it gives way after 1d6 rounds of climbing) with the condition catch chances (a second percentile roll at or above the number means the throw succeeded); with no protrusion in range, recheck after traveling 10 feet vertically or horizontally. Census 368 -> 369.
banner.provenance: the WSG scan (archive.org item pdfy-B3Fz83tZ3TV7zOc8), printed p. 38; the user own copy OCR cross-checked against the archive djvu word layer (Guide_0038.djvu) with IIIF eye-reads - the djvu is garbled at the last Table 20 row (it reads 60/90 m 96 99), at the strength fraction and at the climb bonus; two independent eye-reads of each zone matched the user copy exactly: the last row is 80/90 with 92/99/99, the throw is 1/3 of strength rounded up times 10 feet, and the bonus is a 3-FOOT bonus (the OCR inch mark resolved to the printed foot mark, no plus sign). Every other cell and number matched the djvu clean.
banner.sentinel: The hook throw: 1/3 of strength (rounded up) times 10 feet, one round per attempt, 1d4 rounds to re-coil a miss, 01-05 on a missed throw directly above hits the thrower for 1d6. The Table 20 last row (cliff, smooth, no ledges): protrusion 80/90, catching at 92/99/99 - and a not-solid protrusion gives way after 1d6 rounds of climbing.

consts.name: wghStrengthDivisor
consts.comment: The maximum upward throw is 1/3 of the character strength score, rounded up, times 10 feet.

consts.name: wghFeetPerStrengthUnit
consts.comment: The rounded-up third of the strength score is multiplied by 10 feet - the example strength of 8 throws 30 feet.

consts.name: wghStr8ThrowFt
consts.comment: A character with a strength of 8 can throw the hook toward a protrusion as far as 30 feet above his head.

consts.name: wghHorizontalInclineDeg
consts.comment: A throw on an incline of 30 degrees or less is horizontal.

consts.name: wghSecureWhirlRadiusFt
consts.comment: A secure thrower needs a 10-foot radius of space around himself to whirl the hook in a circle before letting it go.

consts.name: wghSecureHorizontalMult
consts.comment: From a secure position, the horizontal throw goes twice as far as the maximum vertical throw.

consts.name: wghThrowRounds
consts.comment: It takes one round to make a throwing attempt with a grappling hook, regardless of the type of throw.

consts.name: wghRecoilRoundsDice
consts.comment: If the hook misses, the character must spend the next 1d4 rounds coiling the rope, whether for another attempt or to stow the equipment.

consts.name: wghSelfHitRollMax
consts.comment: Throwing at a target directly above oneself: if the throw misses and the die roll was 01-05, the thrower is hit by the hook.

consts.name: wghSelfHitDamageDice
consts.comment: The thrower hit by his own hook takes 1d6 points of damage.

consts.name: wghClimbBonusFt
consts.comment: A climber can climb up a rope anchored by a grappling hook at a 3-foot bonus to his normal climbing movement rate if lightly encumbered or not encumbered.

consts.name: wghNonSolidGiveWayDice
consts.comment: A protrusion between the two Chance of Protrusion numbers is not solid: if snagged, the hook gives way after 1d6 rounds are spent climbing up the rope.

consts.name: wghTerrainCount
consts.comment: Table 20 has ten terrain rows: the three moderate slopes, the three severe slopes and the four cliff types.

consts.name: wghRecheckDistanceFt
consts.comment: If no protrusion exists within throwing range, a character can check for protrusions again after traveling a distance of 10 feet vertically or horizontally.

bools.name: wghAnyClimberCanUse
bools.comment: The grappling hook can be used by any climber - thief or non-thief, mountaineer or non-mountaineer.

bools.name: wghThreeOrFourProngs
bools.comment: A grappling hook is a three- or four-pronged metal hook attached to the end of a rope and thrown toward a protrusion, in hopes that it catches and holds.

bools.name: wghNeededSevereHandyModerate
bools.comment: Hooks are normally only needed for severe slopes and cliff faces, but expedite movement up a moderate slope, especially a slippery or slightly slippery one.

bools.name: wghHorizontalSameAsVertical
bools.comment: A horizontal throw (an incline of 30 degrees or less) has the same maximum distance as a vertical toss, unless the thrower is secure with room to whirl.

bools.name: wghSecurePositionDoubles
bools.comment: In a secure position with a 10-foot whirling radius, the horizontal throw goes twice as far as the maximum vertical throw.

bools.name: wghAboveSelfDangerous
bools.comment: It can be dangerous to throw a hook toward a target directly above oneself - a missed throw rolling 01-05 hits the thrower for 1d6 damage.

bools.name: wghClimbBonusLightOnly
bools.comment: The 3-foot climb bonus on an anchored rope applies only if the climber is lightly encumbered or not encumbered.

bools.name: wghNoMovementBenefitOtherwise
bools.comment: In other cases the rope affords no benefit to movement - except, perhaps, to make upward movement possible where it was not possible before.

bools.name: wghSolidHoldsIndefinitely
bools.comment: A protrusion roll at or above the second Chance of Protrusion number is solid: if the character snags it, the hook will hold indefinitely.

bools.name: wghNotSolidGivesWay
bools.comment: A protrusion roll at or above the first number but less than the second is not solid: if snagged, the hook gives way after 1d6 rounds spent climbing up the rope.

bools.name: wghSecondRollCatches
bools.comment: The Condition of Terrain numbers are the chance of catching a thrown hook on a protrusion, assuming one exists: a second percentile roll at or above the number means the throw was successful.

bools.name: wghRecheckAfter10Ft
bools.comment: With no protrusion within throwing range, a character can check for protrusions again after traveling 10 feet vertically or horizontally.

tables.name: Table 20: GRAPPLING SUCCESS
tables.audit_comment: the Table 20 grid: the ten terrain rows (the three moderate slopes, the three severe slopes and the four cliff types) x the Chance of Protrusion pair and the three condition catch chances - the last row (cliff, smooth, no ledges) is the eye-read row, protrusion 80/90 with 92/99/99
col_comments: The first Chance of Protrusion number, by terrain row: a percentile roll at or above it means a protrusion exists within throwing range.

The second Chance of Protrusion number: a roll at or above it means the protrusion is solid and the hook holds indefinitely; between the two numbers it is not solid and gives way after 1d6 rounds of climbing.
The chance of catching the thrown hook on a protrusion on a non-slippery surface (a second percentile roll at or above the number succeeds).
The catch chance on a slightly slippery surface.
The catch chance on a slippery surface.
